notes: Original documents (kelp, harbor, berth). Not copied from the specification examples. Inputs are UTF-8 text. An empty document is an empty object in the reference decoder.

cases.title: Root string kelp
cases.paragraph: A document may be one primitive. An unquoted token that is not a keyword or a number is a string.

cases.title: Root number 7
cases.paragraph: A decimal integer token decodes as a number. 7 has no fraction and no exponent.

cases.title: Root boolean true
cases.paragraph: The unquoted token true is the boolean true.

cases.title: Root null
cases.paragraph: The unquoted token null is null.

cases.title: Root number 1.5
cases.paragraph: A decimal token with a fraction decodes as a number. 1.5 has no trailing zeros.

cases.title: Exponent token 1e2
cases.paragraph: An exponent form decodes as the number it names. 1e2 is one hundred.

cases.title: Object harbor and n
cases.paragraph: An object is one key and value per line. harbor is a string and n is a number.

cases.title: Boolean and null fields
cases.paragraph: A field value true is a boolean. A field value null is null.

cases.title: Quoted true is a string
cases.paragraph: A quoted token is a string even when the characters spell a keyword. "true" is not the boolean true.

cases.title: Inline array of two strings
cases.paragraph: A primitive array may sit on its header line. The bracket declares the length. Values are separated by the active delimiter.

cases.title: Nested object berth
cases.paragraph: A nested object is indented under its key. The child fields are name and depth.

cases.title: Tabular array of two objects
cases.paragraph: An array of uniform objects declares its fields once. Each following line is one row.

cases.title: Full-line comment
cases.paragraph: A line whose first non-space character is # is a comment. The decoder skips it and reads the object that follows.

cases.title: Empty document
cases.paragraph: A document with no value is an empty object.

cases.title: Unterminated string
cases.paragraph: A quote starts a string. The string is not closed, so the document is not valid.

cases.title: Duplicate key harbor
cases.paragraph: Strict mode rejects a second field with the same key. harbor is written twice.

cases.title: Inline array shorter than its header
cases.paragraph: The header says two values. One value is not that array. Strict mode rejects the count mismatch.

cases.title: Tab used as indentation
cases.paragraph: Indentation is spaces. A tab in the indent is not a nested field. Strict mode rejects it.

cases.title: Tabular row shorter than the field list
cases.paragraph: The header names two fields. A row with one cell does not match that width. Strict mode rejects it.
